A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calsequestrins are Ca(2+ )storage proteins that are synthesized by a limited number of cell types, and that the protein is not a universal component of the endoplamic reticulum of all cell types.

calsequestrins are Ca2+ binding proteins that, in the absence of a specific mechanism to maintain their intracellular distribution, will be eliminated by the cell as soon as their synthesis is induced.

calsequestrins are not essential for the Ca(2+ )release response in epithelial HeLacells, at least when the cells are exposed to the Ca2+ releasing agents used in our experiments, but they can be secreted and possibly play a role in the control of the Ca2+-signalling machinery.
